haiku-low.q1: It gets 401 Unauthorized before any Redis call. No rate-limit counter is read or changed.
haiku-low.q2: Standard customers get 100 requests per minute in total, since all of a customer's keys share one budget. Enterprise is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q3: 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After and no X-RateLimit headers. The backend never sees the request.
haiku-low.q4: No. A request rejected with 429 uses no budget.
haiku-low.q5: Yes. It stays counted, and the client gets the backend's 500 with X-RateLimit-Limit and X-RateLimit-Remaining headers.
haiku-low.q6: Fail open: the gateway forwards the request normally, emits ratelimit_store_unavailable once, and adds no X-RateLimit headers.
haiku-low.q7: Standard allows 100 requests per minute. The Enterprise limit is undecided, has no default, and the gateway will not start without it.
haiku-low.q8: A shared Redis holds counter key rl:{customerId}:{windowStart}. Each key expires 5 seconds after its window ends, which removes old counts.
haiku-low.q9: Counts are per fixed one-minute window on Redis time, so the budget resets when each new window starts.
haiku-low.q10: The Lua script runs as one indivisible Redis step, so no other command runs in the middle of its check and increment.
haiku-low.q11: Seconds left in the window (windowEnd minus Redis time), rounded up, with a minimum of 1.
haiku-low.q12: No retry and no local fallback counter. The client gets no X-RateLimit headers, because the remaining count is unknown.

sonnet.q1: It gets 401 Unauthorized. No rate-limit counter is read or changed (no Redis call).
sonnet.q2: All of a customer's keys share one budget, so in total only the plan limit per minute (100 for Standard; Enterprise number undecided).
sonnet.q3: 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header (and no X-RateLimit headers). The backend never sees the request.
sonnet.q4: No. A 429 uses no budget (nothing is incremented when rejected).
sonnet.q5: Yes. Counting happens before forwarding, so it stays counted and is not refunded.
sonnet.q6: Fail open: the gateway forwards the request to the backend anyway, emits ratelimit_store_unavailable, and adds no X-RateLimit headers.
sonnet.q7: Standard: 100 requests per minute. Enterprise: not decided yet (Product undecided; gateway won't start until it is configured).
sonnet.q8: In one shared Redis, in per-customer fixed one-minute window counters keyed rl:{customerId}:{windowStart}. Each key is set to expire at the window's end plus 5 seconds, so old counters clean themselves up.
sonnet.q9: It resets when the next fixed one-minute wall-clock window starts (a new counter key, based on Redis time).
sonnet.q10: The check-and-increment runs as a Lua script in Redis, which executes as one indivisible step, so no other command runs in the middle.
sonnet.q11: The script returns the seconds left in the window (windowEnd - redisTime), rounded up, at least 1, and the gateway sends it as Retry-After.
sonnet.q12: No retry (also no local fallback counter or circuit breaker). The client gets no X-RateLimit-* headers, just the backend response.
